tools.name: ask_question
tools.description:
# Conversational Research Partner (NotebookLM • Gemini 2.5 • Session RAG)

## No Active Notebook
- Visit https://notebooklm.google to create a notebook and get a share link
- Use **add_notebook** to add it to your library (explains how to get the link)
- Use **list_notebooks** to show available sources
- Use **select_notebook** to set one active

> Auth tip: If login is required, use the prompt 'notebooklm.auth-setup' and then verify with the 'get_health' tool. If authentication later fails (e.g., expired cookies), use the prompt 'notebooklm.auth-repair'.

Tip: Tell the user you can manage NotebookLM library and ask which notebook to use for the current task.

question.description: The question to ask NotebookLM. Plain natural language; can be multi-line. Gemini responds grounded on the notebook's sources.

session_id.description: Reuse an existing browser session for follow-up questions. Pass back the `session_id` returned in a prior `ask_question` response — NotebookLM keeps the prior conversation in context, so follow-ups get sharper. Omit for a fresh session. `list_sessions` enumerates live sessions.

notebook_id.description: Library notebook id (from `list_notebooks` / `search_notebooks`). Defaults to the active notebook (see `select_notebook`) when omitted.

notebook_url.description: Direct NotebookLM URL — overrides `notebook_id`. Use for ad-hoc queries against notebooks not yet in your library. Format: `https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/<uuid>`.

source_format.description:
How citations are returned alongside the answer:
  • `none` (default) — raw answer, no citation extraction (fastest)
  • `footnotes` — answer plus a `Sources:` block, e.g. `[1] DocName — "excerpt…"`
  • `inline` — `[N]` markers in the answer are replaced with `[N] (DocName: "excerpt…")`
  • `json` — answer text untouched; structured `sources` array on the response

Use `none` for snappy chat. Use `json` when downstream code needs to process citations programmatically. Use `footnotes`/`inline` when showing the answer to a human reader.

show_browser.description: Show browser window for debugging (simple version). For advanced control (typing speed, stealth, etc.), use browser_options instead.

browser_options.description: Optional browser behavior settings. Claude can control everything: visibility, typing speed, stealth mode, timeouts. Useful for debugging or fine-tuning.

show.description: Show browser window (default: from ENV or false)

headless.description: Run browser in headless mode (default: true)

stealth.description: Human-like behavior settings to avoid detection

enabled.description: Master switch for all stealth features (default: true)

delay_min_ms.description: Minimum delay between actions in ms (default: 100)

delay_max_ms.description: Maximum delay between actions in ms (default: 400)

tools.name: add_notebook
tools.description:
Register a NotebookLM notebook in the local library so it can be queried with `ask_question`, ingested into with `add_source`, etc.

## Required URL
The user must supply a NotebookLM share-link. To produce one:
  1. Open https://notebooklm.google
  2. Open the notebook → click "Share" (top right)
  3. Set "Anyone with the link" → "Copy link"

## Permission workflow
Do NOT call this tool unprompted. The expected dialogue is:
  1. Ask for the URL
  2. Ask what knowledge it contains (1–2 sentences) → `description`
  3. Ask which topics it covers (3–5) → `topics`
  4. Ask when it should be consulted → `use_cases`
  5. Propose a `name` and the metadata back to the user
  6. Only after explicit confirmation, call `add_notebook`.

Free-tier limits: 100 notebooks · 50 sources each · 50 queries/day. Google AI Pro/Ultra raises these 5×.

url.description: NotebookLM share URL. Format: `https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/<uuid>` (with optional `?authuser=N` suffix).

description.description: 1–2 sentence summary of what the notebook contains.

use_cases.description: When the LLM should consult this notebook, e.g. ['Implementing n8n workflows'].

tools.name: list_notebooks
tools.description: List every notebook in the local library with its metadata (`id`, `name`, `description`, `topics`, `tags`, `url`, `use_count`, etc.). Use the returned `id` for `select_notebook`, `update_notebook`, `get_notebook`, `remove_notebook`, or as `notebook_id` on `ask_question` / `add_source` / audio tools.

tools.name: get_notebook
tools.description: Fetch full metadata for one notebook by id. Use to verify what's currently stored before calling `update_notebook`, or to show the user the exact `description`/`topics`/`use_cases` Claude has for it.

tools.name: select_notebook
tools.description:
Mark a notebook as the active default. After this, `ask_question`, `add_source`, and the audio tools resolve to that notebook when the caller omits `notebook_id` / `notebook_url`.

When to call:
  • The user explicitly switches context (e.g. "Let's work on React now")
  • Task obviously needs a different notebook than the current one — announce the switch ("Switching to the React notebook…") before calling.
  • If the right notebook is ambiguous, ask the user first instead of guessing.

tools.name: update_notebook
tools.description:
Patch metadata fields on an existing notebook. Pass `id` plus any subset of `name`, `description`, `topics`, `content_types`, `use_cases`, `tags`, `url` — only supplied fields change.

Workflow: identify the target notebook → propose the exact change back to the user → call only after explicit confirmation. Multiple fields can be updated in one call.

topics.description: Replacement topics list (full replacement, not append).

tools.name: remove_notebook
tools.description:
Remove a notebook from the local library. **Does NOT delete the actual NotebookLM notebook on Google's side** — only the local metadata entry. Active sessions on this notebook are closed.

Confirmation workflow: look up the notebook by id, ask the user "Remove '[name]' from your library?" — only call after a clear yes.

tools.name: search_notebooks
tools.description:
Search the library by free-text query — matches against `name`, `description`, `topics`, and `tags`. Returns notebook objects with their `id` so you can chain into `select_notebook` etc.

Use this when the user references a notebook by topic ("the React one") instead of by exact name. If multiple notebooks match, propose the top 1–2 and let the user choose.

tools.name: get_library_stats
tools.description: Aggregate statistics about the local notebook library: `total_notebooks`, `active_notebook` (id), `most_used_notebook`, `total_queries`, `last_modified`. Useful as a quick health check or when the user asks "what notebooks do I have?".

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: List all active browser sessions for this server. Each entry includes `id`, `created_at`, `last_activity`, `age_seconds`, `inactive_seconds`, `message_count`, and `notebook_url`. Useful before `reset_session` / `close_session` or to recover a `session_id` you can pass back into `ask_question` to continue an existing conversation. Sessions older than `session_timeout` (see `get_health`) are auto-closed.

tools.name: close_session
tools.description: Permanently close a session and discard its browser tab. Use the `id` returned by `list_sessions` (or the `session_id` from a prior `ask_question` response). Closed sessions cannot be resumed — start a new one with `ask_question` (no `session_id`) or pick another from `list_sessions`. Ask the user before closing if the session might still be needed.

session_id.description: Session id to close. Obtain from `list_sessions` or from any prior `ask_question` response (`result.session_id`).

tools.name: reset_session
tools.description: Clear a session's chat history while keeping the same session id. Use this when the task changes mid-conversation and you want a fresh context without losing the underlying browser tab. Ask the user before resetting if they might still need the prior history.

session_id.description: Session id to reset. Obtain from `list_sessions` or from a prior `ask_question` response (`result.session_id`).

tools.name: get_health
tools.description:
Inspect server state. Returns:
  • `authenticated` — whether saved Google cookies are still valid
  • `notebook_url`, `active_notebook_id`, `active_notebook_name` —
    the currently selected library notebook (or null)
  • `total_notebooks` — library size
  • `active_sessions`, `max_sessions`, `session_timeout` — runtime
    session stats (timeout in seconds; sessions auto-close after this)
  • `headless`, `auto_login_enabled`, `stealth_enabled` — config
Use this first thing in a new conversation. If `authenticated=false`, run `setup_auth` (or `re_auth` to switch accounts).

tools.name: setup_auth
tools.description:
Open a browser window for first-time Google login. Returns immediately after spawning the browser; the user has up to 10 minutes to complete sign-in, then cookies are persisted for future runs.

When to use:
  • `get_health` reports `authenticated=false` for the first time
  • Auto-login credentials are not configured
  • `re_auth` is the right call when you want to *switch* accounts or recover from a daily-quota lockout

After login finishes, call `get_health` to verify success.

If the browser session feels broken (auth keeps failing, stale cookies), run `cleanup_data(confirm=true, preserve_library=true)` first, then retry `setup_auth`.

show_browser.description: Show the browser window. Default: true (must be visible so the user can interact). For advanced control use `browser_options`.

browser_options.description: Advanced browser settings. Override visibility, timeout, or headless mode (default: visible, 30 s).

tools.name: re_auth
tools.description:
Switch to a different Google account or recover from broken auth. Closes all active sessions, deletes saved cookies and Chrome profile, and opens a fresh login browser.

Common triggers:
  • NotebookLM's 50 queries/day free-tier limit is reached and the user wants to rotate to another Google account
  • `setup_auth` failed and a clean slate is needed

After login, call `get_health` to verify. For very stuck states, run `cleanup_data(confirm=true, preserve_library=true)` before `re_auth`.

show_browser.description: Show the browser window. Default: true.

tools.name: cleanup_data
tools.description:
Two-phase deep cleanup of all server data on disk (auth state, browser profiles, caches, MCP logs, temp backups). Cross-platform (Linux/macOS/Windows). Always close all Chrome/Chromium instances first — open browsers can lock files.

Phase 1 (preview): call with `confirm: false`. Returns a categorised list of paths and total size. **No deletion happens.**
Phase 2 (delete): after the user reviews the preview and approves, call with `confirm: true`.

Set `preserve_library: true` to keep the notebook library file (library.json) while wiping everything else — recommended when troubleshooting auth.

Typical recovery flow:
  1. cleanup_data(confirm=false, preserve_library=true)  // preview
  2. cleanup_data(confirm=true, preserve_library=true)   // execute
  3. setup_auth (or re_auth)

confirm.description: false = preview only (default). true = actually delete after user reviewed the preview.

preserve_library.description: Keep notebook library.json while deleting everything else. Default: false. Set true when only auth/browser state is broken.

tools.name: add_source
tools.description:
Ingest a source into a NotebookLM notebook. Supports two source types in v2.0:
  • `url` — NotebookLM crawls and indexes a website
  • `text` — paste raw text (treated as a copied document)

File / YouTube / Google-Drive uploads are not yet implemented.

Returns `sourceCountBefore`/`sourceCountAfter` so the caller can verify the new source landed. Call once per source — multiple sources require multiple calls. NotebookLM finishes indexing within 5–30 seconds; subsequent `ask_question` calls then have the new source in context. Free notebooks cap at 50 sources.

Known quirk: pasted-text uploads occasionally redirect to a freshly created "Untitled notebook" on Google's side. The tool detects this and returns a clear error so you can re-try against the correct URL.

type.description: `url` crawls the supplied website; `text` ingests `content` verbatim as a copied document.

content.description: When `type=url`: a fully-qualified URL (https://…). When `type=text`: the raw text body (any length up to NotebookLM's per-source word limit, ~500 k for free tier).

title.description: Display title shown in the source list. Optional — NotebookLM picks a sensible default (page title for URLs, first line for text). For text sources, supplying a title is recommended for later identification.

show_browser.description: Show the browser window for debugging. Default: false.

session_id.description: Reuse an existing browser session by id. Recommended when you have already called `ask_question` against the same notebook — saves the 10–15 s page-load time. Obtain from `list_sessions` or any prior `ask_question` response (`result.session_id`).

notebook_id.description: Library notebook id (from `list_notebooks` / `search_notebooks`). Defaults to the active notebook (see `select_notebook`) when omitted.

notebook_url.description: Direct NotebookLM URL — overrides `notebook_id`. Use for ad-hoc notebooks not yet in your library. Format: `https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/<uuid>`.

tools.name: generate_audio
tools.description:
Trigger podcast-style Audio Overview generation for a notebook.

**Async by default** — returns immediately with one of:
  • `status: "started"` — generation just kicked off
  • `status: "in_progress"` — a generation was already running; this call attached to it
  • `status: "ready"` (with `alreadyExisted: true`) — an Audio Overview already existed; nothing was triggered

Generation typically takes 2–10 minutes. **Workflow:**
  1. `generate_audio` → returns immediately
  2. Poll `get_audio_status` every ~30 s
  3. When status is `ready`, call `download_audio`

Pass `wait_for_completion: true` for legacy synchronous behaviour (blocks for up to `timeout_ms`). Audio Overview is the only Studio output exposed in v2.0 (Video / Mindmap / Quiz / Infographic / Datatable / Presentation are NotebookLM features but not yet wrapped).

custom_prompt.description: Optional focus prompt for the Audio Overview, e.g. "Focus on the API authentication flow and skip pricing". Passed into the NotebookLM "Customize" sub-dialog before generation starts.

wait_for_completion.description: If true, block until the audio tile is ready (up to `timeout_ms`). Default false — return immediately and let the caller poll `get_audio_status`.

timeout_ms.description: Only relevant when `wait_for_completion=true`. Maximum wait for the audio tile to appear. Default 600 000 (10 min).

show_browser.description: Show the browser window for debugging. Default: false.

session_id.description: Reuse an existing browser session by id. Recommended when you have already called `ask_question` against the same notebook — saves the 10–15 s page-load time. Obtain from `list_sessions` or any prior `ask_question` response (`result.session_id`).

notebook_id.description: Library notebook id (from `list_notebooks` / `search_notebooks`). Defaults to the active notebook (see `select_notebook`) when omitted.

notebook_url.description: Direct NotebookLM URL — overrides `notebook_id`. Use for ad-hoc notebooks not yet in your library. Format: `https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/<uuid>`.

tools.name: get_audio_status
tools.description:
Non-blocking probe for the current Audio Overview state of a notebook.

Returned `status` values:
  • `ready` — Audio Overview is generated and ready to download
  • `in_progress` — generation is currently running
  • `not_started` — no Audio Overview exists yet for this notebook

Safe to poll every ~30 s while waiting for `generate_audio` to finish. When status flips to `ready`, call `download_audio` with a destination directory.

show_browser.description: Show the browser window for debugging. Default: false.

session_id.description: Reuse an existing browser session by id. Recommended when you have already called `ask_question` against the same notebook — saves the 10–15 s page-load time. Obtain from `list_sessions` or any prior `ask_question` response (`result.session_id`).

notebook_id.description: Library notebook id (from `list_notebooks` / `search_notebooks`). Defaults to the active notebook (see `select_notebook`) when omitted.

notebook_url.description: Direct NotebookLM URL — overrides `notebook_id`. Use for ad-hoc notebooks not yet in your library. Format: `https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/<uuid>`.

tools.name: download_audio
tools.description:
Save the completed Audio Overview to disk as a `.m4a` file. **Pre-condition:** `get_audio_status` must report `status: "ready"`. Calling this before generation completes returns an error message explaining what to do.

The file lands in `destination_dir` with NotebookLM's suggested filename (sanitised — usually the audio's title with underscores). The full saved path is returned in `result.filePath`.

destination_dir.description: Absolute directory path where the file is saved (created if missing). Example: `/Users/jane/Downloads/notebooklm` or `/tmp/audio`. Relative paths are NOT recommended — the server may run from a different working directory than the caller.

show_browser.description: Show the browser window for debugging. Default: false.

session_id.description: Reuse an existing browser session by id. Recommended when you have already called `ask_question` against the same notebook — saves the 10–15 s page-load time. Obtain from `list_sessions` or any prior `ask_question` response (`result.session_id`).

notebook_id.description: Library notebook id (from `list_notebooks` / `search_notebooks`). Defaults to the active notebook (see `select_notebook`) when omitted.

notebook_url.description: Direct NotebookLM URL — overrides `notebook_id`. Use for ad-hoc notebooks not yet in your library. Format: `https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/<uuid>`.
